help_text.helpText: This view provides a means to identify potential source analogues for a given target chemical, the centroid of the radial plot. The radial plot displays K source analogues (otherwise called nearest neighbours) where K can be set from 1 to 15. Analogues are pre-filtered based on the availability of in vivo toxicity data.  Analogues are ordered in decreasing order of similarity in a clockwise manner in the plot, starting with the most similar at the top.  The similarity indices are annotated c (for chemistry) or b (for bioactivity) depending on the similarity context selected.  Analogues may be identified using chemical descriptors or bioactivity descriptors. There are 3 different types of chemical descriptors included that are fingerprint representations of chemical structure - Morgan fingerprints, torsion fingerprints and chemotypes. Bioactivity descriptors make reference to a fingerprint representation of hitcalls from the ToxCast assays. For more details watch the video.<iframe width="560" height="225" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/TCg387LhVpY?rel=0&start=246" frameborder="0" allow="autoplay; encrypted-media" allowfullscreen></iframe>

This data matrix view provides a means of performing a data gap analysis of the target chemical and the toxicity outcome for each source analogue represented as red and blue boxes to indicate presence and absence of effects. The view also provides information of the doses at which toxicity effects were observed by hovering over the boxes, which provide a means of assessing the validity of the analogues to determine which should be included in any read-across prediction. The data displayed can be filtered by specific effects or by setting thresholds for number of positives and negatives to be included in any prediction derived. The GenRA prediction is derived by clicking on the Run read-across button. Predictions and their associated confidence scores expressed as AUC values and their p-values can be displayed by hovering and the predictions are coloured coded in the same way as experimental results but by degrees of opacity. The opacity corresponds to how much confidence is associated with a prediction. The data matrix view and any generated predictions can be exported as a tsv or excel file by clicking on the export button. For more details watch the video <iframe width="560" height="300" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/TCg387LhVpY?rel=0&start=559" frameborder="0" allow="autoplay; encrypted-media" allowfullscreen></iframe>

This figure provides a summary representation of the data availability associated with the target chemical and its identified source analogues. The quantity of data associated with a given chemical is indicated by the number of records and the darkness of the associated box. The representation provides a summary overview of the data quantity and coverage for the target and source analogues. This starts to provide a perspective to inform data gaps. For more details watch the video <iframe width="560" height="315" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/TCg387LhVpY?rel=0&start=408" frameborder="0" allow="autoplay; encrypted-media" allowfullscreen></iframe>

This grouping by toxicity data as arising from ToxRefDB and across the Tox fingerprint which provides a representation of the data quantity across different toxicity effects for the source analogues selected. This informs the data gap analysis step of the workflow. Clicking on Generate data matrix launches the final window in the grid view to display a data matrix overview of the target chemical and its source analogues. Selecting the similarity weight on the top bar provides a visual cue of the similarity by adjusting the size of the experimental data box for a given analogue. For more details watch the video <iframe width="400" height="200" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/TCg387LhVpY?rel=0&start=483" frameborder="0" allow="autoplay; encrypted-media" allowfullscreen></iframe>

neighbor_by.description: Morgan fingerprints are also known as extended-connectivity fingerprint ECFP4.  These circular fingerprints are calculated within the RDKit python library as bit vectors with a radius of 3 and a length of 2048.
neighbor_by.name: Chem: Morgan Fgrprts

neighbor_by.description: Torsion fingerprints or hashed topological torsion descriptors are calculated as bit vectors using python's RDKit library. Developed by Nilakantan et al (1986), the topological torsion is defined as a linear sequence of 4 consecutively bonded non-hydrogen atoms, each described by its atomic type, the number of non-hydrogen branches attached to it and its number of pi electron pairs.
neighbor_by.name: Chem: Torsion Fgrprts

neighbor_by.description: ToxPrint Chemotypes are a fixed set of structural features targeted to cover chemical structures from the large toxicity databases and regulatory inventories (Yang et al 2015). Chemotypes use CSRML (chemical substructure and reaction mark-up) language to represent atom-bond connectivity as well as their properties such as pi-systems. The generic structural fragments are organised by atom, bond, chain, ring types as well as chemical groups including amino acids, carbohydrates, ligands and nucleobases based on 729 essential chemotypes of the ToxPrint v2.0_r711.xml.
neighbor_by.name: Chem: ToxPrints

neighbor_by.description: High Throughput Phenotypic Profiling (HTPP, cell painting). This is a fingerprint representation of 1300 features in one of two cell types U2OS or MCF7. Morphological information for each cell, intensity, texture captured as each fluorescent label gives rise to 1300 features. This representation provides a profile/fingerprint that can be used to compare substances with annotated reference chemicals to elucidate potential mechanisms.
neighbor_by.name: Biology: HTPP

neighbor_by.description: ToxCast fingerprints are a non-directional fingerprint representation of assay hit calls represented by the assay component name of the associated platform.  Hit calls are taken from Level 5 of the associated invitrodb. This fingerprint collection comprises both ToxCast and Tox21 assay outcomes.
neighbor_by.name: Biology: ToxCast data

neighbor_by.description: ToxRef fingerprint. This is a fingerprint representation of treatment-related chemical effects derived from ToxRefDB v2. The fingerprint representation is defined by concatenating study type with effect target.
neighbor_by.name: Toxicity: ToxRef data

neighbor_by.description: 2:1:1 Morgan:Torsion:ToxRef hybrid fingerprint
neighbor_by.name: Morg2:Tors1:Bio1

neighbor_by.description: 1:3 ChemoType:ToxCast hybrid fingerprint
neighbor_by.name: CT1:Bio3

The radial plot displays K source analogues (otherwise called nearest neighbours) where K can be set from 1 to 15. Analogues are pre-filtered based on the availability of in vivo toxicity data.  Analogues are ordered in decreasing order of similarity in a clockwise manner in the plot, starting with the most similar at the top.  The similarity indices are annotated c (for chemistry) or b (for bioactivity) depending on the similarity context selected.  Analogues may be identified using chemical descriptors or bioactivity descriptors. There are 3 different types of chemical descriptors included that are fingerprint representations of chemical structure - Morgan fingerprints, torsion fingerprints and chemotypes. Bioactivity descriptors make reference to a fingerprint representation of hitcalls from the ToxCast assays. For more details watch the video.<iframe width="560" height="225" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/TCg387LhVpY?rel=0&start=246" frameborder="0" allow="autoplay; encrypted-media" allowfullscreen></iframe>

This data matrix view provides a means of performing a data gap analysis of the target chemical and the toxicity outcome for each source analogue represented as red and blue boxes to indicate presence and absence of effects. The view also provides information of the doses at which toxicity effects were observed by hovering over the boxes, which provide a means of assessing the validity of the analogues to determine which should be included in any read-across prediction. The data displayed can be filtered by specific effects or by setting thresholds for number of positives and negatives to be included in any prediction derived. The GenRA prediction is derived by clicking on the Run read-across button. Predictions and their associated confidence scores expressed as AUC values and their p-values can be displayed by hovering and the predictions are coloured coded in the same way as experimental results but by degrees of opacity. The opacity corresponds to how much confidence is associated with a prediction. The data matrix view and any generated predictions can be exported as a tsv or excel file by clicking on the export button. For more details watch the video <iframe width="560" height="300" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/TCg387LhVpY?rel=0&start=559" frameborder="0" allow="autoplay; encrypted-media" allowfullscreen></iframe>

For more details watch the video <iframe width="560" height="315" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/TCg387LhVpY?rel=0&start=408" frameborder="0" allow="autoplay; encrypted-media" allowfullscreen></iframe>
